translation.english_title: Long live, long live, long live, long live!

english_lines: Long live, long live, long live, long live!
notes: `அறிஞர்` is retained as the honorific `Arignar` rather than reduced to a generic `scholar`, preserving the source's public/political register.
`அண்ணா` and `குமர அண்ணா` remain source-shaped names/addresses rather than being expanded by inference.

english_lines: Against all those men who boast of greatness,
Who, whatever the matter, like buffaloes,
Go on nodding their heads — for rights,
notes: The buffalo-head-nodding ridicule is retained as an intentionally coarse political image rather than softened to `those who merely agree`.

english_lines: The poor man writhing like a worm,
The grandee flying like an eagle — these,
He made into a golden land where they are no more — that,
notes: The worm/eagle class contrast is kept literal and sharp.
`சீமான்` is rendered as `grandee` to preserve privileged social rank rather than neutralizing it to `rich man`.

english_lines: The widow living like a mouse,
Old custom pouncing like a tiger,
This cruelty that has become so commonplace,
Long live Anna who will change it!
notes: The mouse/sacrifice/tiger accumulation is preserved line by line rather than compressed into a general reform message.
`பழமை` remains `old custom` here so the source's attack on oppressive inherited practice stays direct.

english_lines: A honey-stream speaking many, many ideas,
An ideal history that feeds rational thought —
notes: `பணத்தோட்டம்` and `செல்வக் குமரி... கோட்டம்!` are retained conservatively in transliteration because the source line may carry title/wordplay force that a literalized English phrase would over-interpret.
The doubled `சிலசில / பலபல` pattern remains audible through `here and there / many, many`.
`பகுத்தறிவு` is rendered directly as rational thought; it is not diluted to generic wisdom.

translator_notes: The translation keeps the song's praise, ridicule, class contrast and reform rhetoric in the same register instead of turning it into ceremonial praise prose.
Animal images — buffalo, worm, eagle, mouse, tiger — remain animals because they carry the song's political bite.
Potential title/wordplay expressions in the closing stanza are transliterated rather than silently reinterpreted.
This is a literary source-faithful translation, not a singable adaptation.
